name: Hairline lowering surgery

card.summary: Scalp-advancement surgery that moves the hairline down to shorten a tall forehead; published series are mostly in women, and the scar is the central debate.
card.aka: forehead reduction, scalp advancement, hairline advancement
card.note: Published outcome series are mainly in women with stable hairlines; forum users who are men discuss scar visibility and future hair loss as the main concerns.

quick.overview:
Hairline lowering surgery, also called forehead reduction, is a procedure in which an incision is made along the hairline and the scalp is loosened and pulled forward, so the hair-bearing skin sits lower and the forehead looks shorter. It is described in the plastic surgery literature mainly for women with a naturally high hairline, and as part of facial feminization surgery for transgender women.

On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as an option for people who feel a large forehead throws off facial proportions. Users compare it with hair transplants and with hairstyling, and a recurring theme is how visible the scar is and whether it suits men, who may go on to lose hair.
quick.mechanism: The surgeon makes an incision at or just in front of the hairline, releases the scalp from the underlying tissue, and advances it forward before closing the wound. Published reports describe different incision designs and ways of anchoring the advanced scalp, including sutures tunnelled through bone. A hair transplant over the scar is sometimes added afterwards to disguise it.
quick.risks: Reported risks include a visible or widened scar, numbness, and the limits on how far the scalp can be advanced. Forum users also raise the concern that surgery on a hairline that is still receding may leave the scar exposed later. Published series are small and mostly retrospective, and mostly involve women, so outcomes in men are less well documented.

lead: Hairline lowering surgery, also called forehead reduction or scalp advancement, is a cosmetic procedure that shortens the vertical height of the forehead by moving the hairline forward. A surgeon incises along the hairline, frees the scalp from deeper tissue, advances it and closes the wound [4][6]. Surgeons have described it chiefly for women with a congenitally high hairline and as one component of facial feminization surgery [2][3][4].

Published reports on the operation are mainly case series and technique descriptions. A retrospective review of 29 women treated by one surgeon over 20 years measured photographs before and after surgery [4], and a series of 91 patients described bone-tunnelling suture fixation of the advanced scalp [8]. Other reports cover forehead reduction in women and hair-transplant alternatives for Asian women with high foreheads [9][10].

In looksmaxxing communities the procedure is discussed as a hardmaxxing option for people who attribute a long forehead to hairline position. Users on looksmax.org describe both favourable results and concerns about scarring, and some argue it suits women better than men [12][13].

paras: In hairline lowering, the incision is placed along the front hairline, and the scalp is undermined and moved forward so that the hair-bearing skin covers part of the forehead [4][6]. Surgical reviews describe the aim as reducing forehead height and, in some designs, hiding the resulting scar within or just in front of the hairline [5][6].

Techniques differ in where the incision sits and how it is shaped. A plastic surgery paper on forehead lifting notes that an incision just in front of the hairline shortens the forehead but, unlike deliberate hairline advancement, does not by itself lower the hairline in the way a dedicated procedure does, and that standard brow-lift techniques can raise the hairline [1]. Reports in women describe irregular, hair-bearing-line incisions designed to look natural [4][9].

Most published series involve women with a naturally high hairline who want a shorter forehead [4][9]. A technique description with outcome analysis in female patients reports measured changes in forehead height [9].

Hairline lowering is among the procedures used in facial feminization surgery, where a high or receded hairline and a prominent brow are treated together with frontal bone reshaping and brow lifting [2][3]. A review of 220 consecutive patients describes the broader set of operations in this field [2].

A retrospective review of 29 women operated on by one surgeon reported standardized photograph measurements of the hairline before and after surgery [4]. A series of 91 patients evaluated hairline lowering with bone-tunnelling suture fixation and reported on its effectiveness and safety [8]. A further paper analysed surgical details and outcomes in female patients undergoing aesthetic forehead reduction [9].

Hair transplantation has also been studied as an alternative way to lower the frontal hairline, including a series in Asian women with high foreheads [10], and reviews discuss transplantation techniques in transgender patients [7]. These reports are largely retrospective and uncontrolled, and none is a randomized trial.

The scar along the hairline is the most discussed drawback in the surgical and forum discussion. Reviews of the technique address scar placement and closure as central to the design [5][6]. A user on looksmax.org who describes extensive research argued that scars vary between individuals, can stretch, and may be visible in some lighting or after swimming, and that results shown online may be flattering because of makeup and photography [13]. Another user who had the operation reported a red line during healing that eventually became essentially unnoticeable [12].

Because the operation is mostly described in women, whose hairlines are generally stable, forum commentators argue that in men the possibility of later recession complicates planning; they suggest assessing whether the hairline is stable before any surgical or transplant approach [11][13].

Users on looksmax.org discuss the procedure in guides, personal result threads and cautionary threads. One long guide describes first deciding whether a perceived large forehead comes from the hairline or the face's proportions, then comparing hairstyling, hair transplants and surgery [11]. Result posts describe the operation as helpful but sometimes costly relative to the change achieved [12]. A critical thread argues that for most men it carries drawbacks that surgeons do not emphasise [13]. Other threads discuss cost and low-priced overseas offers, which are mentioned here only as a topic of discussion.

timeline.event: A plastic surgery paper discusses hairline lowering during forehead rejuvenation, noting that standard techniques can raise the hairline [1].
A 20-year single-surgeon review of hairline lowering in 29 women is published [4].
A case report combines hairline lowering with frontal sinus reshaping and brow lift in a transgender woman [3].
A series of 91 patients evaluates bone-tunnelling suture fixation [8].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, hairline lowering is discussed as a hardmaxxing alternative to hair transplants for a long forehead, with debate centring on the scar and on whether it suits men [11][12][13].

claims.claim: A tall forehead is often a hairline issue that surgery can fix.
claims.believers: A guide author says many people blame face shape for a large forehead, though in most cases the hairline is the cause, and a result thread reports a visible improvement after surgery [11][12].
claims.experts: Surgical series in women report measured reductions in forehead height after hairline lowering [4][9].

claims.claim: The scar makes it a poor choice for most men.
claims.believers: A critical thread says scarring varies, can stretch, and is visible in some conditions, and that before-and-after pictures online are flattered by lighting and makeup [13].
claims.experts: Reviews treat scar placement and closure as a central design issue; published series are mostly in women and report acceptable scars, so male outcomes are less documented [4][5][6].

claims.claim: A hair transplant over the scar can disguise it.
claims.believers: Forum users say transplants over the scar are used, though one says graft placement within scar tissue can be a problem [13].
claims.experts: Reviews of hairline lowering and of transplant techniques discuss combining the two approaches [5][7].

claims.claim: The hairline must be stable before any surgical option.
claims.believers: A guide author says to determine whether the hairline is stable or receding first, since a transplant on an unstable hairline may not look good in a few years [11].
claims.experts: A surgical paper notes the concern that surgery can alter hairline position over time, and series mostly describe women with stable hairlines [1][4].
